rules: Each garment is one flat colour area inside a long, smooth key-line contour, heavier than the face's lines (Met 55810, 54869, 37176; CMA 1956.753).
Folds are a few lines from support points running with the fall, ending in a taper or small hook, drawn over the pattern; no shading (Met 55810; CMA 1956.753).
White or plain cloth: folds by blind embossing plus a few lines (CMA 1985.309 label); with no embossing in the engine, lines alone (judgement).
Pattern lies flat: motifs keep one size and shape across folds and turns, crests stay circles, flowers run straight through folds (Met 55810, 55800; CMA 1956.753; Met 55185 Western dress).
Motifs are cut by the outline, overlapping cloth and fold lines, never wrapped round the form (Met 55185, 37176, 55810).

Stripes and checks keep constant spacing: straight within a panel and changing angle at a turn (Met 36922, 55222), or bending gently along a large panel's main fall (Met 55810); never compressed or shaded.
Pattern as its own flat colour or paper reserve on the garment's ground (Met 55800; CMA 1956.753; judgement on block logic).
Layered edges (hem, sleeve, collar) as parallel bands of flat colour, each with its own key line (Met 55800; CMA 1985.309).

Patterned shirt: flat ground, pattern at one motif size over the whole shirt, cut by outline, collar, seams and the apron's edge; fold lines at elbow, armpit and waist over it (judgement applying the pattern rule; Met 55185, 55182).

Apron: a separate flat panel in its own colour with its own contour, overlapping shirt and trousers; ties as key-line loops like obi bows; one or two sag lines over the lap (Met 55800, CMA 1985.309 bows; judgement for the apron).

Seated trousers: flat colour per leg area; knee told by the outline's angle; two or three short compression lines behind the knee and at the groin, one or two long lines down the shin (Met 36922, 36521, 55182; judgement for the seated case).
keep: support points and direction of fall
where cloth bunches (inside a bent knee or elbow)
few big folds over small ones
material told by the contour: soft cloth sags in long curves, stiff cloth breaks at angles
avoid: pattern foreshortened, compressed or shaded round the form
fold lines that interrupt or hide the pattern instead of lying over it
a soft, painterly hem or contour
